name: Dal Baati Churma
description: Baked wheat balls (baati) dunked in ghee, served with spiced lentils (dal) and a sweet crushed-wheat churma — the signature meal of Rajasthan.

name: Laal Maas
description: A fiery Rajput mutton curry coloured deep red with Mathania chillies — historically a hunter's dish.

name: Pyaaz Kachori
description: A flaky deep-fried pastry stuffed with spiced onions, a Jodhpur and Jaipur breakfast staple.

name: Sarson da Saag & Makki di Roti
description: Slow-cooked mustard greens topped with white butter, served with cornmeal flatbread — the winter soul-food of Punjab.

name: Amritsari Kulcha
description: A crisp, stuffed and tandoor-baked bread served with chole and butter, an Amritsar icon.

name: Punjabi Lassi
description: A thick, sweet churned-yogurt drink topped with a dollop of malai (cream), served in a tall glass.

name: Lucknawi (Awadhi) Biryani
description: A delicate dum-cooked biryani of fragrant rice and meat, milder and more perfumed than its Hyderabadi cousin.

name: Tunday Kababi
description: Melt-in-the-mouth minced-meat galouti kebabs from Lucknow, said to use over a hundred spices.

name: Banarasi Paan
description: A betel-leaf preparation with gulkand and areca, the traditional after-meal ritual of Varanasi.

name: Litti Chokha
description: Roasted wheat balls stuffed with spiced sattu (roasted gram flour), served with mashed brinjal-potato-tomato chokha — Bihar's defining dish.

name: Silao Khaja
description: A layered, flaky deep-fried sweet from Silao near Nalanda, crisp and soaked in syrup.

name: Chandni Chowk Chaat
description: The tangy street-food universe of aloo tikki, gol gappe and dahi bhalla in Old Delhi's lanes.

name: Butter Chicken
description: Tandoori chicken in a rich tomato-butter gravy, invented in Delhi's Moti Mahal and now world-famous.
